feedback: Integration note from the controller side. Iteration 0 (entityR2B) shows 60 of 60 trials ended off_track, with max_error at about 0.062 to 0.064 m (the 0.06 m limit) and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. The robot drifts to the edge and loses the tape before it recovers. To work with the current 10 mm sensor pitch, I had to keep weights proportional to x (the controller could not compensate for a layout that gives little signal range). With your proposed spread of +/-0.03 m and 15 mm pitch, the same weights give about one third less signal per metre of offset, so I have raised kp to restore steering gain. Your widened spread is the right direction given the line-loss and max_error evidence. Keep the 12 mm footprint for now: 12 mm footprints with 15 mm pitch still overlap the 25 mm tape near centre. Hold the lead at y = 0.05 unless steering oscillation at speed shows a problem. Once the next race reports, decide as follows. If line_loss_events fall and max_error drops below 0.06, keep the spread and treat any remaining issue as controller tuning. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more while max_error is still at the limit, the sensors are not the main cause, so hold the geometry and move to a larger footprint.
requested_changes: Keep the +/-0.03 m spread (x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03) with 12 mm footprints and y = 0.05 for the next race. The iteration 0 evidence (max_error about 0.062 and 1 to 2 line-loss events in every run) supports the wider coverage, and changing both the spread and the footprint at once would hide which change helped.

If line_loss_events remain at 1 or more and max_error is still at 0.06 after the race, try sensor_size 0.016 (16 mm footprints) to give the outer sensors more tape overlap at the edge, keeping the same positions.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 at the new gain, move the sensors forward to y = 0.06 to 0.07, keeping the spread. Do not change the lead while line loss is still the main failure.
